item.title: #1 [0/100] Longitudinal viral load trajectories predict cervical lesion risk in women with persistent human papillomavirus infection: A prospective cohort study.

Authors: Zhou Y, Chen S, Zhang Y, Jiang Y, Xiao M, Xin X, Shi Z, Zhang L
Journal: Cancer | DOI: 10.1002/cncr.70648
Published: 2026-Dec-01
PMID: 43069728



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is central to cervical lesion development, but single viral-load measurements may not capture heterogeneous viral dynamics. This study characterized longitudinal viral-load trajectories among women with persistent infection and evaluated their associations with cervical lesions and incremental predictive value beyond baseline factors. METHODS: In this prospective cohort of 1502 HPV-positive women followed at approximately 6-month intervals, latent class growth analysis using actual follow-up time was conducted among 624 women with type-specific persistent infection. Associations between trajectory group and any cervical lesion (low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion [HSIL]) were assessed using multivariable logistic regression; HSIL was explored using Firth-penalized regression. Discrimination, calibration, and decision-curve analysis were used to assess incremental predictive performance. RESULTS: Of 1170 women with classifiable outcomes, 624 had persistent infection. Four trajectories were identified: low stable (39.6%), moderate declining (18.9%), moderate increasing (29.8%), and persistently high (11.7%). Any-lesion prevalence was 10.9%, 17.8%, 74.2%, and 90.4%, respectively (p < .001). Compared with the low-stable group, fully adjusted odds ratios (ORs) were 1.95 (95% CI, 1.02-3.74), 29.66 (95% CI, 16.75-52.51), and 124.29 (95% CI, 47.30-326.60) for the other groups, respectively. The persistently high group was also associated with HSIL (OR, 9.47; 95% CI, 3.18-33.09). The optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) increased from 0.713 for the base model to 0.888 for both the simple longitudinal and trajectory models and 0.899 for the joint model. CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal HPV viral-load dynamics identified clinically distinct risk phenotypes. Moderate-increasing and persistently high trajectories were strongly associated with cervical lesions, whereas longitudinal information improved discrimination beyond baseline measurements. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

item.title: #2 [0/100] Intensity-controlled Raster Scanning Carbon Ion Radiation Therapy With a Heavy-ion Gantry: Clinical Experience at Heidelberg Ion Beam Therapy Center.

Authors: Dvornikovich K, Held T, Franke H, Cakir C, Dörsam L, Manzey T, Jiang ZC, Winter S, Sittinger M, Winter M, et al.
Journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics | DOI: 10.1016/j.ijrobp.2026.09.003
Published: 2026-Dec-01
PMID: 43044650



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Carbon ions have biophysical advantages over photons, including a finite range, increased relative biological effectiveness, and lowered oxygen dependence. Maximum treatment flexibility is attainable with rotational beam delivery. We report our clinical experience using the carbon-ion gantry at the Heidelberg Ion Beam Therapy Center with intensity-controlled raster scanning capability, focusing on treatment toxicity. METHODS AND MATERIALS: A total of 1622 patients treated using the carbon-ion gantry between 2012 and 2026 were evaluated. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Toxicity analysis was conducted using Common Terminology Criteria of Adverse Events v5.0. RESULTS: The median age preradiation therapy was 59 years (range, 18-91). Most patients had locally advanced tumors (21.8% T4; 11.2% T3) without regional lymph node metastases (45.4% N0). The most common treatment indications were sacrococcygeal tumors (n = 331; 20.4%), followed by tumors of the paranasal sinuses (n = 166; 10.2%) and the spine (n = 121; 7.5%). A total of 486 patients (30.0%) received carbon-ion reirradiation, the most frequent carbon-ion gantry treatment indication viewed across all patients. The most common particle therapy beam-angle number was 2 (range, 1-7). The use of more than 2 beam angles was particularly frequent in tumors of the skull base (45.8%) and the thoracic region (40.0%). High-grade (III and IV) acute and late toxicity rates were 2.4% and 4.2% in primary treatment. Mean numbers of acute and late grade I and II toxicity events per patient were 2.2 (95% confidence interval, 2.0-2.4) and 2.0 (95% confidence interval, 1.7-2.4), respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Carbon-ion radiation therapy using a heavy-ion gantry resulted in favorable toxicity rates in specific indications. Further interdisciplinary research demonstrating the clinical benefit of carbon-ion radiation therapy is required. This study provides more evidence supporting particle therapy facilities and may serve as a foundation for prospective clinical trials.

Authors: Schaefer J, Son L, Fang Z, Walvekar RR
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70562
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43076213



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stage at diagnosis is a strong predictor of survival in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). Gulf South population-level data on these disparities remain limited. METHODS: We analyzed 1344 patients with known stage at diagnosis from Louisiana Tumor Registry data (n = 1698 cases, 2018-2023). Geographic access was operationalized as straight-line distance from parish centroid to the nearest academic medical center (AMC), categorized as < 25, 25-50, and > 50 miles. Multivariable logistic regression examined predictors of advanced-stage presentation (Stage III-IV) and nodal burden (N2-N3). RESULTS: Advanced-stage disease increased with distance from AMC (33.8%, 38.7%, 46.6%; Mantel-Haenszel χ2 = 13.4, p = 0.0003). Distance > 50 miles independently predicted advanced-stage presentation (OR 1.56, p = 0.008) and high nodal burden (OR 1.44, p = 0.030). Black race (OR 2.25), Medicaid (OR 1.62), and smoking (OR 2.91) were independent predictors. HPV-positive histology was strongly protective (OR 0.33, p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Distance from specialty care independently predicts advanced-stage OPSCC and extensive nodal disease even after controlling for HPV status, race, insurance, and socioeconomic factors, supporting targeted teleoncology expansion and rural outreach initiatives.

item.title: #4 [0/100] Blinded Evaluation of Patient-Facing Thyroid Cancer Information From Clinicians, Large Language Models, and Web Search.

Authors: Hack S, Karni RJ, Coblens O, Hayu D, Sonnino R, Minkowitz G, Krinsky D, Locatello LG, Malkin BD, Rivero A, et al.
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70497
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43076196



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the quality of patient-facing thyroid cancer information generated by clinicians, large language models (LLMs), and web search results using parallel expert and layperson evaluation under blinded conditions. STUDY DESIGN: Blinded comparative evaluation study. SETTING: Online, text-based assessment of patient-facing health information. METHODS: Thirty commonly searched thyroid cancer questions were identified using Google Trends. For each question, patient-facing answers were generated by a fellowship-trained head and neck surgeon, 5 widely used LLMs (GPT-4, GPT-5, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek), and the first nonsponsored Google search result. Responses were anonymised and source-blinded. Seven attending physicians evaluated responses using the Quality Analysis of Medical AI (QAMAI) framework across 5 domains, and 15 lay participants evaluated the same responses across 4 patient-centred domains. Ratings were analysed at the question level using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Friedman tests, Kendall's W, and post-hoc Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. RESULTS: Expert inter-rater reliability was good across domains (ICC 0.78-0.82). Expert ratings differed significantly across sources (P < .001; Kendall's W = 0.70-0.81), with Claude achieving the highest expert scores and Google-derived responses the lowest. Layperson ratings also differed significantly (P < .001; Kendall's W = 0.70-0.87) but clustered near the upper end of the scale, indicating a ceiling effect. The largest expert-rated differences occurred for treatment-related questions, particularly radioactive iodine therapy. CONCLUSION: Patient-facing thyroid cancer information quality varies across clinicians, LLMs, and web search results. Divergence between expert and layperson assessments indicates that perceived clarity and reassurance do not reliably reflect expert-defined completeness or clinical robustness.

Authors: Lin EY, Zhou AS, Grey S
Journal: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology | DOI: 10.1177/00034894261511058
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43075940



Abstract:
Nasal septal perforation (NSP) is a known complication of nasal trauma such as surgery or cauterization, intranasal drug use, autoinflammatory or autoimmune conditions, and infection. Cryoglobulinemic vasculitis (CV) is a less common cause of NSP in which immune complexes precipitate in and occlude small vessels, leading to ischemic necrosis of the nasal septal mucosa. This is a case report of a 75-year-old female patient with monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) and associated type I CV who presented with longstanding, recurrent bilateral nasal crusting, and was found to have a large anterior NSP with normal-appearing margins. Given her otherwise unremarkable medical or social history, her presentation was most likely attributable to the known CV. Biopsy to rule out malignancy was deferred, and it was anticipated that there would significant improvement in sinonasal symptoms with treatment of the underlying conditions. Therefore, the patient was initiated on low dose prednisone with subsequent taper, in addition to pre-existing plasma cell-directed therapy and dexamethasone, and the nasal crusting and drainage significantly improved after 2 weeks without need for surgical intervention.

Authors: Kajal S, Chopra P, Bajaj D, Gandicheruvu H, Halawi A, Kazemizadeh Gol MA, Ashley W
Journal: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology | DOI: 10.1177/00034894261510589
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43075931



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pneumocephalus typically results from craniofacial trauma, tumors, infections, or skull base defects. Acute pneumocephalus in a patient without prior neurological history or obvious skull base defects presents a diagnostic challenge. CASE PRESENTATION: A 65-year-old male with a history of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and multiple esophageal dilations post-radiation presented with hypercapnic respiratory failure. He developed acute-onset altered mental status after initiation of Bilevel Positive Airway Pressure (BiPAP). An urgent head computed tomography (CT) scan showed pneumocephalus, and subsequent sinus CTs showed no skull base defects. Nasal endoscopy showed no obvious clear fluid drainage, and nasal secretions tested negative for beta-2 transferrin. Retrospective review of a chest CT from 3 months prior revealed a small proximal esophageal defect with prevertebral air tracking. Follow-up CT imaging confirmed air tracking along the T1 costovertebral joint, identifying an enterothecal fistula as the route for positive-pressure air entry into the spinal canal and cranial vault. The pneumocephalus resolved within 10 days with conservative measures. Although surgical obliteration of the fistula was discussed, the patient opted against surgical intervention. CONCLUSION: Spontaneous or positive-pressure-induced pneumocephalus without a skull base defect should prompt investigation of alternative air-entry pathways, including enterothecal fistulas, particularly in patients with predisposing risk factors such as esophageal malignancy and dilations.

Authors: Service CA, Jones ACM, Anderson B, Chia PH, D'Souza AN, Davies LM, Di Luca B, Hoogenhout L, Koehl EM, Leslie E, et al.
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70554
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43075817



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Royal Melbourne Hospital implemented an Enhanced Recovery After Surgery program with prehabilitation (ERAS+) for patients undergoing head and neck (HN) surgery with free flap (FF) reconstruction. This study evaluated the feasibility of ERAS+. METHODS: Feasibility was assessed using Bowen's Framework in patients undergoing HN surgery with FF reconstruction between May 2023 and August 2024. Clinical outcomes were compared with a historical cohort treated before ERAS+ implementation (January 2022 to January 2023). RESULTS: ERAS+ achieved high prehabilitation uptake (91%) and attendance (90%). Patient satisfaction was high (90%-96%), and compliance with ERAS protocols improved by 22.1%. Median hospital length of stay was 2 days shorter within the ERAS+ cohort (15 vs. 17 days; p = 0.115). Postoperative complications, return to surgery, readmission, time to decannulation, time to oral intake and 28-day survival were similar between groups. CONCLUSIONS: ERAS+ implementation was feasible and improved perioperative pathway compliance, with no clear impact on length of stay or complication rates.

Authors: Degirmenci N, Ozdem A, Firat CK, Yakut K, Aksoy T, Ozturan O
Journal: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology | DOI: 10.1177/00034894261508742
Published: 2026-Nov-23
PMID: 43074183



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Periostin is a matricellular protein implicated in structural tissue changes and chronic inflammation. Adenoid hypertrophy (AH) is thought to be driven by chronic inflammatory stimulation, in which recurrent antigen exposure promotes lymphoid hyperplasia and persistent enlargement of adenoid tissue. However, the molecular mediators contributing to adenoid tissue remodeling remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to evaluate serum and tissue periostin levels in children with AH. METHODS: This prospective controlled study included children aged 2 to 8 years. The study group consisted of children with grade 3 to 4 AH scheduled for adenoidectomy, while the control group comprised children with grade 1 AH without clinically significant disease. Serum and tissue periostin levels were compared. RESULTS: Serum periostin levels were significantly higher in children with AH compared with controls (P = .019). In addition, periostin concentrations were significantly increased in adenoid tissue compared with paired normal nasopharyngeal mucosal tissue (P = .016). CONCLUSION: The findings of this study demonstrate that periostin levels are elevated both systemically and locally in children with AH. This elevation suggests that periostin-associated inflammatory and remodeling pathways may play a role in the pathophysiology of AH. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04152746.

Authors: Zhang T, Ding C, Cheng X, Yang C, Zheng D, Chen K
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362355
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43071660



Abstract:
Rapid urbanization and large-scale village demolition in China have erased many traditional rural settlements from the physical landscape, but not from residents' memories. How to reconstruct these invisible spaces and sustain local culture in the absence of material fabric remains an underexplored question in rural sustainability research. This qualitative case study focuses on Shixinzhuang, a demolished village now occupied by the new campus of Zhengzhou University in central China. We conducted in-depth oral history interviews with six long-term residents selected through purposive sampling based on native attachment, spatial role, and generational span. During interviews, participants drew cognitive maps starting from their own courtyards to locate streets, public facilities, production zones, and ritual spaces. Hand-drawn maps were systematically organized and compared to identify shared spatial patterns and memory discrepancies. This information was further cross-verified through data triangulation with archival photographs, satellite imagery, field revisits, and focused validation discussions. Data analysis centered on themes of spatial memory, memory places, and cultural sustainability. Findings indicate that despite the complete demolition of the physical village, Shixinzhuang's spatial structure can still be systematically reconstructed from villagers' memories. Residents consistently recalled the village's evolution from a walled enclosure to an open, expanding settlement. Its spatial organization was structured around a "cross-street" skeleton formed by a north-south main street and an east-west auxiliary street, with housing in the central area growing organically while peripheral housing was more orderly. Spatial memories were highly clustered around several "memory places," notably the Nainai Miao (Grandmother Temple), ancestral grave areas, and residential rooftop platforms. Even after relocation, these places continue to carry kinship ties, religious rituals, and neighborhood interactions. Furthermore, production spaces reflected layered institutional experiences transitioning from collective agriculture to a marginal industrial belt, with distinct intergenerational differences emerging in narratives differentiating between "collective labor" and "earning money in the brick kilns." Ultimately, the joint process of narration, mapping, and iterative correction transformed the oral history practice from a unidirectional recording into a reflexive, participatory act of "re-creating place." This study demonstrates that even when a traditional village has disappeared from the ground, its spatial structure and symbolic places can be recovered through the combined use of oral history and cognitive mapping, and mobilized as resources for rural cultural sustainability. For demolished settlements, integrating narrative-based spatial reconstruction into planning, heritage management, and community-building can help re-anchor local identity, inform commemorative and interpretive design, and institutionalize residents' narrative participation in rural spatial governance.

Authors: Ope MS, Ashrafuzzaman M
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0356864
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43071659



Abstract:
The rising issue of fungicide resistance, along with environmental concerns related to synthetic fungicides, highlights the need for safer and more sustainable antifungal agents. In this computational study, we screened nineteen phytochemicals from locally available medicinal plants in Bangladesh against three fungal protein targets associated with major wheat diseases: class I sesquiterpene synthase (PDB ID: 8H4P) and trichothecene 3-O-acetyltransferase (TRI101; PDB ID: 3B2S) from Fusarium graminearum, and the AvrSr50 effector protein (PDB ID: 7MQQ) from Puccinia graminis f. sp. tritici. Blind docking was performed using AutoDock Vina (with an exhaustiveness setting of 16) and evaluated for reliability through consensus docking with CB-Dock2. We analyzed protein-ligand interactions using BIOVIA Discovery Studio, and the top-ranked compounds were further assessed for toxicity and ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity) properties with ProTox-3 and ADMETlab 3.0. Thevetin B, Thevetin A, and Uscharin were computationally prioritized as candidate multitarget binders. Notably, Thevetin B formed extensive hydrogen-bond and hydrophobic interaction networks across all three proteins and showed comparatively strong predicted binding affinities. However, ProTox-3 predicted high acute oral toxicity for Thevetin B (LD₅₀ = 4 mg/kg, Class I) and Thevetin A (LD₅₀ = 8 mg/kg, Class II), while Uscharin had a substantially higher predicted LD₅₀ (2000 mg/kg, Class IV). The ADMET analysis revealed shared liabilities such as mutagenicity and nephrotoxicity, along with limited absorption, but also highlighted compound-specific differences in physicochemical properties and environmental toxicity. These findings indicate an efficacy-safety trade-off among the computationally prioritized candidates and support their further evaluation as testable hypotheses rather than establishing a definitive efficacy-safety hierarchy. This study provides a structured computational prioritization of locally available phytochemicals and emphasizes that any claims of practical antifungal utility must be supported by experimental validation of both efficacy and safety.
